properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 8198375
Permit API: 065-26269
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2024
Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.As of today the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts and waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. As I was leaving the Wheeler sites, I ran into Ray Hepler. He stated that the contaminated soil from the clean-up was added to the same truck containing soil from the southwest, and that he would eventually be providing tipping an manifest information. Mr. Hepler also stated he was unfamiliar with an Act 2 clean up. I told him I would email information about Act 2 when I returned to the office. The outstanding violations for this well will remain open.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.
Violation ID: 8228893
Permit API: 125-29133
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Blaine Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/09/2025
Comments: On April 9, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit was issued by the Department for the site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad and upslope of the northern corner of the well pad, which was reported to the Department by the operator on April 7, 2025. Range Resources representative Dennis Furmanek was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Stimulation operations are ongoing at the well pad at the time of this inspection (see photos 3 and 18). All containers onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within well pad secondary containment (see photo 20). All secondary containment onsite appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection with no holes or tears observed. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 23). The GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 24). Some areas of minor staining were observed on the surface of the well pad during this inspection. The E and S inspection log, E and S plan drawings, Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan, E and S individual permit approval letter, secondary containment inspection, log, and well permits are onsite (see photos 19 and 25). Upon review onsite, the ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 2). The soil crack that was reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present on the southwestern fill slope of well pad (see photos 4-9). It appears to be approximately 15 feet in length with saturated ground down slope of it, and no toe bulge observed below at the time of inspection. The Schwotzer to Hoskins pipeline is being constructed west of the well pad (see photo 11). The slough that was also reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present up slope of the northern corner of well pad (see photos 12-16). The operator estimates this area of soil movement to be approximately 25 feet wide by 30 feet long. This slough appears to pose the potential to threaten a stormwater channel down slope of it, if the displaced soil continues to move (see photo 17). Mr. Furmanek reported during this inspection that the operator intends to conduct repairs on these areas of soil movement once stimulation operations have been completed onsite and weather conditions allow for it. CFS that appears to be in need of maintenance was observed along the northeastern edge of the well pad (see photo 21).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends the operator conduct general maintenance and housekeeping onsite to address the minor staining onsite and CFS maintenance needed. The Department also recommends that the operator monitor the soil crack on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on the soil exposed by the slough north of the well pad.Violations shall be issued against the slough north of the well pad which could pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. See NOV Response Comments.

Comments: On April 9, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit was issued by the Department for the site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad and upslope of the northern corner of the well pad, which was reported to the Department by the operator on April 7, 2025. Range Resources representative Dennis Furmanek was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Stimulation operations are ongoing at the well pad at the time of this inspection (see photos 3 and 18). All containers onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within well pad secondary containment (see photo 20). All secondary containment onsite appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection with no holes or tears observed. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 23). The GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 24). Some areas of minor staining were observed on the surface of the well pad during this inspection. The E and S inspection log, E and S plan drawings, Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan, E and S individual permit approval letter, secondary containment inspection, log, and well permits are onsite (see photos 19 and 25). Upon review onsite, the ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 2). The soil crack that was reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present on the southwestern fill slope of well pad (see photos 4-9). It appears to be approximately 15 feet in length with saturated ground down slope of it, and no toe bulge observed below at the time of inspection. The Schwotzer to Hoskins pipeline is being constructed west of the well pad (see photo 11). The slough that was also reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present up slope of the northern corner of well pad (see photos 12-16). The operator estimates this area of soil movement to be approximately 25 feet wide by 30 feet long. This slough appears to pose the potential to threaten a stormwater channel down slope of it, if the displaced soil continues to move (see photo 17). Mr. Furmanek reported during this inspection that the operator intends to conduct repairs on these areas of soil movement once stimulation operations have been completed onsite and weather conditions allow for it. CFS that appears to be in need of maintenance was observed along the northeastern edge of the well pad (see photo 21).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends the operator conduct general maintenance and housekeeping onsite to address the minor staining onsite and CFS maintenance needed. The Department also recommends that the operator monitor the soil crack on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on the soil exposed by the slough north of the well pad.Violations shall be issued against the slough north of the well pad which could pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. See NOV Response Comments.

Comments: On 01/13/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 01/02/2026 at the NV48 Well Site. The Department first received notification of the spill 01/09/2026 from CNX (CTS 39456). I was accompanied by Ralph Barb (PA DEP), Melissa Cherry of Penn E and R, SPSI, and CNX representative Joe Fletcher.Per CNX, spill was said to have been reported to the Departments emergency hotline on 01/02/2026 via the 1 (800) 541-2050 phone number, however the Department did not have a history of a notification. Justin Ruth of CNX submitted a call log of the call, which occurred at 5:48 PM on 01/02/2026.On 01/09/2026, Chad Eisenman of CNX notified the Department of the spill; it was reported that 5 bbls of combined brine and freshwater released onto the pad at the NV48 Well Site on 01/02/2026. The spill was identified at approximately 3:48 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 5:58 PM. Soil and gravel were impacted on the pad, the spill was contained to the pad, and no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. CNX is utilizing the alternative spill remediation standards under Act 2.The following was observed during inspection:The spill originated from two produced water tanks (brine) on containment, and a freshwater tank. Produced fluid back-fed into the freshwater tank, and the combined fluids released out of the freshwater tank onto the pad. 5 barrels (bbls) were released (Photo 1).The majority of the impacted material on the pad has been remediated. The impacted area furthest from the tanks yielded conductivity readings ranging from 98.6 - 551 S/cm (Photos 2-6).The surface material was scraped and removed, and trenches/sumps were dug. Conductivity readings within the trenches yielded readings ranging from 1148 S/cm - 3.46 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).Conductivity readings closer to the tanks and the front section of the impacted area ranged from 1469 S/cm - 7.41 mS/cm (Photos 12-18).The area was still in the process of remediation; however it was anticipated to be done the day of the Departments inspection (Photos 19-21).A background conductivity reading was obtained near the edge of the pad. The reading was 655 S/cm (Photos 22, 23).It was noted on site that the roll off dumpster was the fifth one to be used for the waste. I observed incorrect labeling on the roll off (Photo 24).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan were both at the site entrance (Photo 25).Due to the release of production fluid combined with freshwater over a barrel, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

I was accompanied by Ralph Barb (PA DEP), Melissa Cherry of Penn E and R, SPSI, and CNX representative Joe Fletcher.Per CNX, spill was said to have been reported to the Departments emergency hotline on 01/02/2026 via the 1 (800) 541-2050 phone number, however the Department did not have a history of a notification. Justin Ruth of CNX submitted a call log of the call, which occurred at 5:48 PM on 01/02/2026.On 01/09/2026, Chad Eisenman of CNX notified the Department of the spill; it was reported that 5 bbls of combined brine and freshwater released onto the pad at the NV48 Well Site on 01/02/2026. The spill was identified at approximately 3:48 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 5:58 PM. Soil and gravel were impacted on the pad, the spill was contained to the pad, and no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. CNX is utilizing the alternative spill remediation standards under Act 2.The following was observed during inspection:The spill originated from two produced water tanks (brine) on containment, and a freshwater tank. Produced fluid back-fed into the freshwater tank, and the combined fluids released out of the freshwater tank onto the pad. 5 barrels (bbls) were released (Photo 1).The majority of the impacted material on the pad has been remediated. The impacted area furthest from the tanks yielded conductivity readings ranging from 98.6 - 551 S/cm (Photos 2-6).The surface material was scraped and removed, and trenches/sumps were dug. Conductivity readings within the trenches yielded readings ranging from 1148 S/cm - 3.46 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).Conductivity readings closer to the tanks and the front section of the impacted area ranged from 1469 S/cm - 7.41 mS/cm (Photos 12-18).The area was still in the process of remediation; however it was anticipated to be done the day of the Departments inspection (Photos 19-21).A background conductivity reading was obtained near the edge of the pad. The reading was 655 S/cm (Photos 22, 23).It was noted on site that the roll off dumpster was the fifth one to be used for the waste. I observed incorrect labeling on the roll off (Photo 24).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan were both at the site entrance (Photo 25).Due to the release of production fluid combined with freshwater over a barrel, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a compliance evaluation inspection of Blackhill Energy's Kline A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 12/26/2023 at 0950 hours. The weather was 41 degrees with cloudy skies and light rain. An Act 9 sign remains in place at the site entrance. Environmental Trainees Erica Lutz and Evan Buck accompanied me during the inspection.On 11/30/2023 elevated conductivity fluids were observed outside of secondary containment summarized in inspection report #3655668. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

Comments: On 10/16/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 10/12/2023 (IR 3630018, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Paul Stiner of Diversified. On 10/12/2023, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued as outstanding for the observed elevated conductivity and the access road condition. The following was observed during inspection on 10/16/2023:The operator had removed impacted soils within the bottom portion of the berm, adjacent to the valve of tank 4. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 1-6). The operator had placed the impacted soils within buckets that were dated (Photos 7, 8).Some soils were removed from the berm adjacent to tank 5. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 9, 10).Regarding the area behind tank 5, it appeared as though the area I initially discovered to have elevated readings, and the operator was not able to replicate my readings, displayed adequate readings on 10/16/23, most likely due to dilution from rain (Photos 11, 12). There was one reading of 3.29 m/S, however this area was small, approximately a 4 inch by 4 inch section (Photo 13). The operator is going to remove some soils from this area, which was marked with a brick (Photo 14). Due to the size of this area, no violation is being noted.The operator explained that the cause of the impacted berm was due to fluids reaching the ground during tank clean out (Photos 15, 16). It is highly recommended to place containment/grate to collect any residual fluids and prevent them from reaching the ground and berm during tank clean out.The access road appeared to remain in poor condition (Photos 17, 18). On 10/13/2023, I had emailed Daniel Frick of Diversified regarding the start time of repairs; Diversified is waiting on bids and can hopefully update me next week (from 10/13 email). As of 10/16/2023, there has not been an update. Also in this email, I had asked if the NOV response for IR 3620008, mentioning the removal of a 5 gallon bucket, was referring to the area under the valve of tank 4 instead of behind tank 5, which was then confirmed to be correct - the material was removed from under the valve. Due to the operator's effort to remediate the impacted areas and the impacted areas appearing in relatively good condition, the violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, and SWMA 301, regarding the release of production fluid, are being closed. Violations of 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a), regarding the access road, remain outstanding.
